items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?
items.rationale: The paper explicitly discusses adoption challenges, learning risks, tool-integration challenges, scaling issues, future work, and that the study is initial.
evidence: ASSOCIATED CHALLENGES: Integration among the models and tools, and other engineering artifacts, is another challenge associated with MBSE.
FUTURE WORK: The work presented in this article is an initial study and modeling to evaluate the effectiveness of the MBSE approach for our satellite design projects.
CONCLUSION: The SysML learning curve is steep.

items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The case is NSS-1, an ongoing remote-sensing student satellite in PNSSP, with lifecycle phases and MBSE artifacts mapped from requirements through AIT.
evidence: OBJECTIVES: we selected an ongoing remote sensing (RS) student satellite (NSS-1) as a case study.
ADOPTED MBSE METHODOLOGY maps Phase 0/A, Phase B, Phase C, and Phase D to project activities and SysML artifacts.
MODEL REPOSITORY FOR NSS-1: The modeling repository uses SysML to capture common design patterns of the typical nanosatellite class.

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?
items.rationale: The paper names OOSEM, SysML 1.4, MagicDraw 18.1, ParaMagic, MATLAB SMT, Excel, InterCAX, diagram types, equations, and the NSS-1 system/subsystem boundary.
evidence: OBJECTIVES: We used MagicDraw 18.1 from No Magic Inc. and SysML 1.4 as the modeling language.
ADOPTED MBSE METHODOLOGY: We have adopted an OOSEM-based hybrid approach.
SYSML MODEL OF THE NSS-1 SATELLITE describes package, requirement, BDD, IBD, use-case, parametric, state-machine, and sequence diagrams.

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Most outcomes are tied to SysML requirement diagrams, parametric diagrams, model repositories, traceability matrices, plug-in interfaces, and generated reports.
evidence: INTRODUCTION: MBSE provides a consistent and automatically traceable system design, which enhances the quality of traceability and change impact assessment.
Requirement Diagram section links requirement diagrams to traceability, verification matrices, and automated impact analysis.
Automatic Report Generation section links SysML models to allocation tables, requirement tables, and coverage analysis.

items.question: Is evidence provided for claimed outcomes, such as metrics, baseline comparison, case-study results, executable simulation results, model checks, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration/test results, or flight/operational data?
items.rationale: The case provides parametric analysis values and tool-flow demonstrations, but broad claims about risk, productivity, quality, cost, and reliability lack baseline comparison, stakeholder evaluation, test, or flight evidence.

items.question: Are model availability, open-source assets, reusable packages, data exchange mechanisms, or sufficient implementation details reported to assess reproducibility and toolchain continuity?

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The study is a credible and detailed SysML/OOSEM small-satellite case with clear lifecycle artifact mapping, traceability, and a worked mass/power verification example. Evidence is weaker for broad value claims and reproducibility because no baseline, open model, or integration/flight validation is reported.

RQ1.rationale: The paper shows general SysML modeling of a nanosatellite-class mission repository and common design patterns, but it does not explicitly address modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge and treats EPS mainly as an abstract power-budget block.

RQ2.rationale: It claims traceability, consistency, productivity, interoperability, knowledge transfer, and a reliability-budget capability, but reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes are mostly system-level and not demonstrated as EPS-specific effects.

RQ3.rationale: Verification is integrated through SysML verify relationships, parametric constraints, and ParaMagic/MATLAB solving for mass and power before physical development; EPS-specific component tests or hardware verification are not reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: No prior extraction or external lineage was consulted. Within the paper, the authors report reusing some FireSat model elements and positioning their work relative to CubeSat/remote-sensing satellite MBSE studies.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_lifecycle_gates: Phase 0/A uses mission scenarios, mission requirements, use-case and requirement diagrams to reach a requirements baseline; Phase B uses packages, BDDs, IBDs, use cases, parametrics, and trade studies to reach baseline system design; Phase C uses subsystem/unit breakdown and behavioral diagrams for detailed design; Phase D uses test cases and V&V for assembly, integration, and testing.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The work is centered on SysML/OOSEM but enhances a conventional SE process with parametric solving, traceability, generated documentation, and interfaces to Excel/MATLAB/STK rather than replacing the whole workflow with a pure MBSE or mature enterprise digital thread.
tailoring_rationale: OOSEM fits the evolutionary nature of the organization's projects and life cycles.
OOSEM supports integration with object-oriented software, hardware, and testing.
OOSEM supports system-level reuse and design evolution.
More OOSEM resources were available than for other candidate methodologies.
A hybrid approach lowers adoption barriers for engineers used to conventional documents and tools.

RQ1: A SysML/OOSEM repository can represent nanosatellite-class missions through requirements, architecture, behavior, interfaces, and parametric packages.

Generality is supported by common nanosatellite design patterns, FireSat reuse, extensible blocks, package organization, and parametric constraints, but the approach still requires SysML/tool/OOP and spacecraft-domain knowledge.
EPS is modeled only at abstract system power-budget/electrical-architecture level, not as detailed EPS behavior or components.
RQ2: Claimed benefits include traceability, change-impact assessment, documentation consistency, automated reports, interoperability, knowledge transfer, reduced risk, quality/productivity, and a reliability-budget capability.

Evidence is strongest for system-level mass/power model execution and tool data flow; reliability outcomes, reproducibility through open assets, and EPS-specific integrability/reliability effects are not demonstrated.
Reproducibility is limited by absence of an open model repository and reliance on proprietary tools/plugins.
RQ3: Requirements are linked to verification artifacts through SysML verify relationships and constraint blocks.
Pre-physical verification is demonstrated by ParaMagic/MATLAB SMT solving of mass and power budget constraints, yielding positive margins for the NSS-1 requirements.
AIT/V&V test-case support is mapped in the methodology, but no EPS-specific physical integration or test results are reported.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The work is an initial study and modeling effort to evaluate MBSE effectiveness.
Future training of system engineers in SysML, its development environment, and object-oriented modeling is needed.
The SysML learning curve is steep and may require software engineering/OOP knowledge.
SysML diagrams may be misinterpreted if not learned beforehand.
Integration among analysis, hardware, software models, tools, and engineering artifacts is a challenge.
Scaling the modeling effort to larger projects and diverse development environments is challenging.
Direct STK-SysML interfacing is future work.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No open model repository, data package, or reusable SysML library is reported.
EPS is represented as a subsystem in power-budget equations, but no EPS component-level behavior, modes, failure modes, or hardware architecture is modeled in detail.
Reliability budget is mentioned but not shown, solved, validated, or connected to EPS reliability outcomes.
Broad risk, productivity, quality, cost, and time-saving claims lack quantitative baseline comparison.
Verification evidence is limited to a simplified mass/power parametric calculation and does not include integration, environmental, flight, or operational data.
Exact publication venue title is not visible in the Markdown.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: we selected an ongoing remote sensing (RS) student satellite (NSS-1) as a case study and developed its SysML model repository.
We used MagicDraw 18.1 from No Magic Inc. [16] as the modeling tool and SysML 1.4 as the modeling language.
We have adopted an OOSEM-based hybrid approach that leverages object-oriented techniques and a SE foundation.

The modeling repository uses SysML to capture common design patterns of the typical nanosatellite class: managing values, describing scenarios, and describing functions, parts, and subsystems, as well as the relationships among these design patterns.
Mass, power, and reliability budgets have been incorporated.

The ACS (Attitude control subsystem), CDHS (Command and data handling subsystem), payload, TCS (Thermal control subsystem), and RFCS (Radio frequency communication subsystem) subsystems draw electrical power from the EPS (Electrical power subsystem), which can supply a maximum of 80 W.
After connecting the parameter ports to respective inputs and outputs, we validated the model using ParaMagic.

We can see that mass and power budget margins are calculated to be positive (mass_MOS=0.082 and power_MOS=0.47), which verify the mass and power requirements as given in the requirement diagram (Figure 12).
MagicDraw provide an interface to import and export data between the SysML model and Microsoft Excel files.
The SysML learning curve is steep.
